title: [smartswitch] monit and dualtorNeighborCheck failures on DPU hosts during post-test health checks
author: vvolam
body:
## Description

After switch reload/reboot operations on SmartSwitch platforms, post-test DPU health checks fail because `monit` and `dualtorNeighborCheck` services report non-OK status on DPU hosts. These failures are reported by `check_dpu_critical_processes()` in `tests/smartswitch/common/device_utils_dpu.py` which runs `sudo show system-health detail` on each DPU and treats any non-OK service as a failure.

## Error

```
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'monit' has failed in DPU0
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'monit' has failed in DPU1
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'monit' has failed in DPU2
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'monit' has failed in DPU3
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'dualtorNeighborCheck' has failed in DPU0
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'dualtorNeighborCheck' has failed in DPU1
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'dualtorNeighborCheck' has failed in DPU2
ERROR    root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'dualtorNeighborCheck' has failed in DPU3
```

These failures occur repeatedly during `test_dpu_status_post_switch_config_reload`, `test_dpu_status_post_switch_mem_exhaustion`, and `test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic` in `tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_reload_dpu.py`.

## Root Cause

The `check_dpu_critical_processes()` function at `device_utils_dpu.py:465` SSHes into each DPU, runs `sudo show system-health detail`, and iterates over all entries. If any entry has `status != "ok"` and is not in `DPU_CRITICAL_PROCESS_SKIP`, it returns `False`.

The current skip list (`DPU_CRITICAL_PROCESS_SKIP`) includes:
```python
frozenset({"container_checker", "snmp", "acms:acms", "routeCheck",
           "PSU0", "PSU1", "PSU2", "PSU3"})
```

But `monit` and `dualtorNeighborCheck` are **not** in the skip list. After a switch reload, these services on DPU hosts may take additional time to converge or may not be applicable to DPU environments at all:

- **`monit`**: The monit daemon on DPU hosts may be in a transient failure state after a switch-level reload. On some DPU platforms, monit may not be fully applicable.
- **`dualtorNeighborCheck`**: This check verifies neighbor reachability for dualtor configurations. On DPU hosts, this check may not be relevant or may fail because the dataplane has not fully converged after a switch reload.

## Affected Tests

- `test_dpu_status_post_switch_config_reload`
- `test_dpu_status_post_switch_mem_exhaustion`
- `test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic`

All in `tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_reload_dpu.py`.

## Suggested Fix

### Option A: Add to skip list (test-side fix)

Add `monit` and `dualtorNeighborCheck` to `DPU_CRITICAL_PROCESS_SKIP` in `device_utils_dpu.py`:

```python
DPU_CRITICAL_PROCESS_SKIP = frozenset({
    "container_checker", "snmp", "acms:acms", "routeCheck",
    "PSU0", "PSU1", "PSU2", "PSU3",
    "monit", "dualtorNeighborCheck",
})
```

### Option B: Buildimage fix

If `dualtorNeighborCheck` is not applicable on DPU hosts, it should be disabled in the DPU monit configuration at the buildimage level.

### Option C: Increase convergence timeout

If these services eventually recover, increase the `wait_until` timeout for `check_dpu_critical_processes` after reload operations.

## Environment

- Platform: Cisco 8102-28FH-DPU-O SmartSwitch
- DPU type: AMD Pensando DSC
- SONiC release: 202511
- Test files:
  - `tests/smartswitch/common/device_utils_dpu.py` (check logic, line 465)
  - `tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_reload_dpu.py` (affected tests)

linkedPullRequests.title: [config reload] Skip routeCheck monit calls on DPU platforms
linkedPullRequests.author: vvolam
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### What I did

On DPU platforms (pensando, nvidia-bluefield), the `routeCheck` monit service is removed from the monit config (sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#26214) since route checking is not applicable on DPUs. However, `config reload` unconditionally tries to `monit unmonitor/monitor routeCheck`, causing:
```
Disabling container and routeCheck monitoring ...
There is no service named "routeCheck"
```

Added a `_monit_service_exists()` helper and guarded `routeCheck` monit calls in `_stop_services()` and `_restart_services()` so they only execute when the service is present in monit.

#### How I did it

- Added `_monit_service_exists(service)` helper that runs `sudo monit summary <service>` and returns `True`/`False` based on exit code.
- In `_stop_services()`: only call `monit unmonitor routeCheck` if `_monit_service_exists("routeCheck")` returns `True`.
- In `_restart_services()`: only call `monit monitor routeCheck` and `_wait_for_monit_service_monitored("routeCheck")` if the service exists.

#### How to verify it

1. On a DPU platform (nvidia-bluefield / pensando) with routeCheck removed from monit config:
   - Run `config reload -y` — should complete without `"There is no service named routeCheck"` error
2. On a non-DPU platform where routeCheck exists in monit:
   - Run `config reload -y` — routeCheck monitoring should still be disabled/re-enabled as before

#### Previous command output (if the output of a command-line utility has changed)

On DPU with routeCheck removed from monit:
```
root@sonic-dpu-3:/home/admin# config reload -y
Acquired lock on /etc/sonic/reload.lock
Disabling container and routeCheck monitoring ...
There is no service named "routeCheck"
Released lock on /etc/sonic/reload.lock
```

#### New command output (if the output of a command-line utility has changed)

On DPU with routeCheck removed from monit:
```
root@sonic-dpu-3:/home/admin# config reload -y
Acquired lock on /etc/sonic/reload.lock
Disabling container monitoring ...
...
Enabling container monitoring ...
Released lock on /etc/sonic/reload.lock
```

Companion PR: sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#26214
Fixes: sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#26225

linkedPullRequests.title: Disable routeCheck, dualtorNeighborCheck and vnetRouteCheck in monit config on DPU platforms
linkedPullRequests.author: vvolam
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

routeCheck, dualtorNeighborCheck and vnetRouteCheck monit checks are not applicable on DPU hosts:
- **routeCheck** verifies routes between APPL-DB and ASIC-DB, which are not relevant on DPUs.
- **dualtorNeighborCheck** verifies neighbor/tunnel route entries for dualtor configurations, which don't exist on DPUs.
- **vnetRouteCheck** verifies VNET routes consistency between SONiC and vendor SDK DBs, which is not applicable on DPUs.

When monit runs these checks on DPU hosts, they report failures that cause post-test DPU health checks to fail with errors like:
```
ERROR root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'dualtorNeighborCheck' has failed in DPU0
ERROR root:device_utils_dpu.py:499 'routeCheck' has failed in DPU0
```

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/26225

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Remove `routeCheck`, `dualtorNeighborCheck` and `vnetRouteCheck` entries from the monit `sonic-host` config during image build for DPU platforms (pensando, nvidia-bluefield) using sed in `sonic_debian_extension.j2`.

Each sed command matches the comment line (e.g. `# route_check.py`) through the next blank/whitespace-only line, deleting the entire monit check block. The sed range terminator uses `^[[:space:]]*$` instead of `^$` for robustness against trailing whitespace.

**Companion PR:** https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4405 — guards `monit unmonitor/monitor routeCheck` calls in `config reload` so they don't fail on DPU platforms where routeCheck is removed.

#### How to verify it

1. Build a SONiC image for a DPU platform:
   ```bash
   make configure PLATFORM=nvidia-bluefield
   make target/sonic-nvidia-bluefield.bin
   ```
2. On the built image, verify the monit config no longer contains the removed checks:
   ```bash
   grep -E "route_check|dualtor_neighbor_check|vnet_route_check" /etc/monit/conf.d/sonic-host
   ```
   Should return no output.
3. Verify monit runs without errors:
   ```bash
   sudo monit summary
   ```
4. Verify non-DPU platforms are unaffected (e.g. `PLATFORM=broadcom` image still has all three checks).

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [x] 202511
